title: Coherent inverse over a nerve with only identity isomorphisms
statement: Use quasicategories, nerves of ordinary categories, coherent functors, functor equivalences and coherent natural equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Work in fixed universes containing the data. Let $B$ be an ordinary category in which every isomorphism is an identity, and put $S=N(B)$. Let $p:X\to S$ and $q:Y\to S$ be coherent functors from quasicategories and let $F:X\to Y$ satisfy $qF=p$ as simplicial maps. Suppose $F$ is a functor equivalence, so that there are a coherent quasi-inverse $G:Y\to X$ and coherent natural equivalences $GF\simeq\mathrm{id}_X$ and $FG\simeq\mathrm{id}_Y$. Then these same data satisfy $pG=q$ as simplicial maps, and each unit and counit equivalence projects to the constant identity transformation of $p$ or $q$. In particular $F$ is an equivalence over the fixed simplicial base $S$. For any simplicial set $K$ in the ambient universe and specified $a:K\to S$, postcomposition of these inverse data gives a functor equivalence between the simplicial sets of functors $K\to X$ and $K\to Y$ with composite exactly $a$ and transformations over its identity, whenever these simplicial sets are quasicategories. No fibration hypothesis is needed for the strict-base identities.
